taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Vitis cinerea but separates the Central Texas Heller's-grape concept as Vitis berlandieri. Older broad V. cinerea records can therefore mix modern concepts.
look_here_first: Treat this as a taxon-concept check. Strict V. cinerea has angled hairy/cobwebby branchlets, cordate usually shallowly lobed leaves with visible gray-green lower surfaces, and small black berries that are only slightly glaucous.

project_inclusion.target_zone_status: UNRESOLVED TAXON CONCEPT — USER APPROVED LEARNER INCLUSION
project_inclusion.range_basis: Current review retains only a strict-concept Hays record as project evidence. Broad Central Texas species-level records may include the historical Heller/berlandieri concept and are not counted.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification. Preserve the concept/range HOLD and do not convert broad legacy records into a PASS.

best_field_traits: strict concept branchlets densely short-hairy and cobwebby
cordate leaves usually unlobed to shallowly 3-shouldered
lower leaf surface gray-green and visibly hairy rather than opaque white-felted
berries black, roughly 4–8 mm, slightly or not glaucous
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Central Texas Heller's grape should not be called V. cinerea simply because an app uses a broad concept; compare with V. berlandieri first.

comparisons.key_distinctions: V. berlandieri is the major concept trap; V. mustangensis has an opaque white-felted underside and larger fruit; V. palmata is red-stemmed, deeply lobed, and nearly glabrous beneath.
